messages.subject: Doubts about parboot function
parts:
Dear group members,

 

I am facing difficulties in interpreting the parboot. I am currently running occupancy models and I am trying to assess the goodness-of-fit through the parboot function (from the unmarked package). I read in Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology, that p values should not be extreme (close to zero or one), however, I do not know what extreme values are. For example, are 0.92 and 0.13 extreme values? How do I interpret parboot results? 


 

Best regards,

Isabella

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Doubts about parboot function
parts:
Dear Isabella,

I think that if you adhere to the traditional significance testing philosophy leading to a black-and-white conclusion about the fit of a model, then anything smaller than 0.05 would indicate an ill-fitting model. However, one ought to be just as wary about too good a fit as about a too badly fitting model. Hence, too large values are also suspect. Thus, anything outside of an interval 0.05 - 0.95 (or perhaps outside of 0.025 - 0.975 ?) would indicate an ill-fitting model.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: Doubts about parboot function
parts:
Dear Isabella,

I suggest you to use the mb.gof.test function (AICcmodavg package), instead of parboot. It is beyond my understanding, but I had test the fit of different models using the parboot and it always showed a good fit; which makes me feel uncomfortable. The mb.gof.test computes the gof test described by MacKenzie and Bailey (2004).

Best regards,
Simón
